 Grammy Awards 2027: See the list of nominees
 By Lisa Respers France , David Mack 
 Updated Nov 16, 2026, 9:14 AM ET 
 PUBLISHED Nov 16, 2026, 7:41 AM ET 
 Raye is the most nominated artist for the upcoming Grammy Awards. 
 Rich Polk/Billboard/Getty Images

 Nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards were unveiled on Monday, with a new generation of female musicians leading the honorees, but big-name icons like Paul McCartney, Madonna, The Rolling Stones and the late Dolly Parton also received ample recognition.
 The British singer-songwriter Raye became this year’s most nominated performer, scoring 11 nods, while Spanish artist Rosalía and country star Ella Langley weren’t far behind, with nine and seven nominations, respectively.
 Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers all received seven nominations apiece, while Bruno Mars, Leon Thomas and Olivia Dean (last year’s best new artist) received six nods.
 Also making history? Beyoncé, who scored an astonishing 100th Grammy nomination. Already the most-nominated artist in Grammys history, Queen B’s latest nod was for the song “Morning Dew (Donk)” in the Best R&B Solo Performance category.
 This year’s ceremony will be broadcast live on ABC and streamed simultaneously on Hulu and Disney+ from Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on February 7.
 A selection of nominations can be found below. The full list of nominees can be found on the Recording Academy website .
 ALBUM OF THE YEAR
 Olivia Rodrigo got seven nominations. 
 Chris Pizzello/Invision/AP

 “The Art of Loving” - Olivia Dean
 “Dandelion” - Ella Langley
 “The Romantic” - Bruno Mars
 “This Music May Contain Hope.” - Raye
 “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love” - Olivia Rodrigo
 “Lux” - Rosalía
 “The Life of a Showgirl” - Taylor Swift
 SONG OF THE YEAR
 “Berghain” (Rosalía, Björk, Yves Tumor)
 “Choosin’ Texas” (Ella Langley)
 “The Cure” (Olivia Rodrigo)
 “Hate That I Made You Love Me” (Ariana Grande)
 “I Knew It, I Knew You (From ‘Toy Story 5’)” (Taylor Swift)
 “Man I Need” (Olivia Dean)
 “Risk It All” (Bruno Mars)
 “Where Is My Husband!” (Raye)
 RECORD OF THE YEAR
 “Man I Need” - Olivia Dean
 “Choosin’ Texas” - Ella Langley
 “I Just Might” - Bruno Mars
 “Where Is My Husband!” - Raye
 “The Cure” - Olivia Rodrigo
 “Berghain” - Rosalía, Björk, Yves Tumor
 “The Fate of Ophelia” - Taylor Swift
 “Dracula” - Tame Impala, Jennie
 BEST NEW ARTIST

 Don Toliver
 Remi Wolf
 The Womack Sisters

 Olivia Dean, who won best new artist last year, got six nods. 
 Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images

 “Risk it All” - Bruno Mars
 “Where is My Husband!” - Raye
 “The Cure” - Olivia Rodrigo
 “Sauvignon Blanc” - Rosalía

 “Bring Your Love” - Madonna, Sabrina Carpenter
 “Click Clack Symphony.” - Raye, Hans Zimmer
 “The Life of a Showgirl” - Taylor Swift, Sabrina Carpenter
 “Dracula” - Tame Impala, Jennie
 BEST RAP ALBUM
 Don Toliver was nominated for best rap performance, best rap album and best new artist. 
 Paras Griffin/Getty Images

 “Bully - Deluxe” — Kanye West (Ye)

 “Erritime” - Cardi B
 “Run It Back” - De La Soul featuring Nas
 “Let ’Em Know” - T.I.
 “Body” - Don Toliver
 BEST TRADITIONAL COUNTRY ALBUM
 “Clovis” - Charley Crockett
 “50 Years from Home: Down at the Borderline” - Vince Gill
 “Banks of the Trinity” - Cody Johnson
 “Workin’ Man: Willie Sings Merle” - Willie Nelson
 “Once Upon a Second Time Around” - Charlie Worsham

 Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" took the charts by storm this year.

 “Dry Spell” - Kacey Musgraves
 “Can’t Sit Still” - Lainey Wilson

 “Your Favorite Toy” - Foo Fighters

 “Frozen Charlotte” - Jack White

 “What’s Wrong with Me” - Olivia Rodrigo, Robert Smith
 “In the Stars” - The Rolling Stones

 “Kehlani” - Kehlani

 Tems was nominated for their performance of "What You Need."
